title: Installation, GOPATH, workspace and the `go` command

videos.script: Lesson 2 told the story of Go's releases. This lesson puts one of them on your machine, and it is the one the rest of the course runs on. {{paths}} There are three ways to get a Go. You can install it. You can run it inside a virtual machine or a container. Or you can type into a web page. One of them is recommended, and each one costs your computer something different. {{install}} Then the install itself. One archive, one directory, and two lines in a file your shell reads when you log in. After that, the go command tells you where everything it owns is kept. {{env}} Next comes GOPATH. It used to decide where your code had to live. Now it holds downloads and installed programs, and your code can live anywhere. A workspace lets two of your own modules use each other before either is published. {{work}} Last, three ways the setup fails, each with its exact message and its fix. That is where most people give up, so it is worth seeing before it happens to you. {{fail}}
